newsitem.title: FRENCH GUIANA: Ariane launches satellites for Arab bloc, Malaysia.
newsitem.headline: Ariane launches satellites for Arab bloc, Malaysia.

text.p: Western Europe's 92nd Ariane rocket placed into orbit satellites for the 21-nation Arab League and Malaysia after a textbook launch from equatorial French Guiana late on Wednesday.
The Ariane 44L rocket equipped with four liquid strap-on boosters -- the most powerful in the Ariane-4 series -- blasted off at 7:40 p.m. (2240 GMT).
The rocket lifted off into a partly cloudy equatorial night sky at the European Space Agency (ESA) launch center in Kourou, French Guiana on the northeast coast of South America.

Twenty minutes after takeoff space officials said the ARABSAT 2B satellite separated from the rocket. The 2.6 ton satellite will provide direct-to-home satellite television, audio and data broadcasting throughout Arab League countries and Arab-speaking nations in the Middle East, North Africa and Southern Europe.

"Arabsat is a great leap forward for Arab League countries, for its technology, development and communiciations among Arab speaking peoples," Arabsat director general Saad Al Bidnah told a pre-launch news conference.

The satellite was built by a consortium led by France's Aerospatiale and is designed to operate in space for 16 years. Arabsat officials estimated the value of the satellite, launch and insurance to be in excess of $200 million.
Five minutes later, MEASAT 2, Malaysia's second satellite designed to give the East Asian country strong multimedia capabilities in the booming Asian market, separated from the rocket.

"MEASAT means Malaysia East Asia Satellite ... We hope MEASAT will revolutionize telecommunications in Malaysia as well as in the rest of Asia," said Tun Mohamed Hanif Omar, chairman of the Kuala Lumpur-based satellite operator Biniariang.
Biniariang is a joint venture among local Malaysian shareholders and the "Baby Bell" company U.S. West, which holds a 20 percent stake.
Company officials said the insured value of the satellite and launch was in excess of $100 million.
The satellite was built in Los Angeles by Hughes Space and Communications.
Wednesday's launch was the fifth Ariane mission since the failure on June 4 of an Ariane-5 rocket, the first of a new generation, 37 seconds after its maiden launch.

It was the 10th Ariane-4 successfully launched this year by the Paris-based Arianespace company that controls more than half of the world's commercial satellite launch market with firm orders to launch 40 heavy satellites worth $3.4 billion.
